# Cluster P (0xc0880-0xc6470): the R300 pixel-shader ("PSN" native format) decoded-instruction optimiser. A "decoded program" is {+0 count, +4 temp count, +8 -> array of 0xa0-byte entries}; one entry = two 0x40-byte halves (RGB at +0x00, alpha at +0x40: +4/+6 dest reg and write mask, +8.. three 4-byte source slots, +0x28 opcode, +0x30 flags) plus six ushort source-address slots at +0x80..+0x8a and a mode word at +0x8c (0 = R100-style words, 1 = R200-style, 2 = R300 US words).

column5: for both halves of a decoded entry: clears the per-source read-mask words (+0x14..+0x24), then re-derives them from the three source slots (address-select bits 0x300, component swizzle fields, opcode class bit-set 0x1f1) and the flags at +0x30; called after every edit by c0fd0/c1780/c1e90/c2834/c3100/c3240/c38a0/c3fd0/c42f0

merges source-address slots that hold the same address (0x80 vs 0x82/0x84 compare, then clears the select bit ^1/^3), turns opcode 5 and 7 forms with identical operands into opcode 0 (mov) and swaps commutative operands; calls psnDecRecomputeSourceUsage when anything changed

memsets the 0x80 header of a decoded entry and unpacks one hardware instruction into it according to the mode word at +0x8c: mode 0 = RS instruction (one dword at wordsMode0[index*4+4]), mode 1 = TEX (nothing decoded), mode 2 = ALU (the four R300 US register images at +0x98 / +0x198 / +0x298 / +0x398: RGB_ADDR, ALPHA_ADDR, RGB_INST, ALPHA_INST, each holding 6-bit address fields); the mode values match psnDecodedToProgram, which writes mode 0 as PSN kind 1 (RS), 1 as kind 2 (TEX) and 2 as kind 3 (ALU); the compiler inlined psnDecRecomputeSourceUsage and psnDecCanonicalizeEntry at the end

swaps address slots a and b (ushort at (group*3+i)*2+0x80) of one group unless a source of the entry is pinned (flag 0x10 or non-zero masks at +0x20/+0x60), then renumbers every source slot selecting that group (select bits 0x300 == (group+1)*0x100)
bubble-orders the three address slots of a group (compares +0x80/+0x82/+0x84, swaps through psnDecTrySwapAddressSlots) and recomputes the usage when any swap happened

for every entry of the decoded program: packs dest/sources/opcode back into the hardware instruction words (mode 0 words at param_2+4.., mode 1 words at param_3+0x18..), the inverse of psnDecDecodeHwInstruction

walks the entries from the last to the first with a stack of free temp indices (the 4 reserved at start, then count..0), assigns the lowest free temp to each destination whose first use is seen, drops entries with no write/side effect (memcpy compaction), stores the new count and temp count, then calls psnDecEncodeHwWords
true for a low-nibble mask equal to 1, 2, 4 or 8 only
true when the entry's alpha half writes (flag 8 in +0x46) the register in param_2 (+0x44)
scans the source slots of both halves for register param_2 whose usage mask has the alpha bit (8) set
scans every source usage mask (entry +0x14 stride) intersecting param_2 against the address slots equal to param_3 over both halves and three slots
like psnDecAnySourceIsReg but requires the usage mask to overlap param_2 without being equal to it (partial component use)
removes from param_2 the components written by the RGB dest (+4/+6) and the alpha dest (+0x44/+0x46) when they target register param_3 and returns whether nothing is left
index (0..2) of the first of the three group-1 address slots (ushort at +0x86..) that is 0xffff, or -1
boolean of psnDecFirstFreeAddressSlot >= 0

for both halves rewrites every source slot that reads register param_2 at address param_5 so that it reads register param_3 through select param_4 (writes the new address into the slot table), then recomputes usage and re-canonicalises when mode 2

replaces address param_2 of the sources reading register param_6 by param_3: counts which slots other operands use (aiStack_58[6] table), frees unused slots (0xffff), finds a free slot for param_3 and rewires the slot selects; returns 0 and restores the old address when none is free
true when a source usage mask of the entry overlaps param_3 for a source slot whose address is register param_2
true when a source slot at address param_2 has a usage mask that overlaps param_3 but also uses components outside it
true when either half's dest register (+4) equals param_2 and its write mask (+6) overlaps param_3
true when none of the three source selects of half (param_2 == 8 picks alpha) selects the fixed slot 3 and the other half's flag 0x20 is clear and param_3 is not 1 or 2
swaps address slots param_2 and param_3 (the group chosen by param_4) in the table at +0x80 and rewrites every source select (bits 0-1) of that group accordingly

saves the 0xa0-byte entry (memcpy to the stack), frees unused address slots, rebinds an address through psnDecSwapAddressSlotsInSources, recomputes and canonicalises, and memcpy-restores the saved entry when the result is rejected (return 1 only on success)
checks bit param_4 of the 64-bit mask (param_2:param_3) and that every component selected by param_5 of the constant at param_1+param_4*16 equals the float at 0x1aa108

walks entries param_3-1 down to param_2 and returns 1 as soon as one reads or writes the destination registers (+4/+6, +0x44/+0x46) of entry param_3, or one of its source registers, via psnDecReadsRegMask/psnDecDestMatchesRegMask; 0 when the range is clear

for two mode-2 entries counts the sources of each that use the group-0/group-1 selects (0x100/0x200) and, when both counts stay below 4, copies the free address slots of one entry into the other (0xffff slots at +0x80/+0x86 receive the other's address) and rewrites the selects; returns 0 when no slot is free

converts a PSN program (records of 0x48 bytes after the header; kind at +0: 1 RS, 2 TEX, 3/4 ALU) into decoded entries (decodedProgram[2] + n*0xa0, mode word +0x8c = 0 RS, 1 TEX, 2 ALU): memset 0x80 each, copies the register / mask / swizzle / opcode / modifier byte fields of the record into the two halves, then runs psnDecRecomputeSourceUsage and psnDecCanonicalizeEntry

inverse of psnProgramToDecoded: memsets each destination PSN record (0x48 bytes), reads the decoded entries (0xa0 stride, mode word +0x8c) and writes kind-2 (TEX) / ALU records with their byte fields back

switch over the 0..0x13 RGB operand select code: 0/4/8/0xf r or no change, 1/5/9/0x10 -> 1, 2/6/10/0x11 -> 2, 3/7/0xb/0x12 -> 4, 0xc-0xe/0x13 -> 8; ORs the component bit into a usage mask when (param_2 & 7)
same idea for the alpha-side select codes 0..0xf (groups 0/3/6/0xc -> 1, 1/4/7/0xd -> 2, 2/5/8/0xe -> 4, 9/10/0xb/0xf -> 8), guarded by mask bit 8

register allocator step: looks up the (virtual register, mask) pair in the sorted interval table, clears the mask bits, and returns the physical register to the sorted free list (memmove insert) once no component is still in use

register allocator step: records a (register, mask) definition in the interval table (marks the entry 0xffff if it was empty), pulls the lowest free physical register from the free list and splits/compacts the list entries
walks a PSN program's records (0x48 stride from param_2+8 count) with two interval tables (_memset of 8*count bytes) and renumbers every TEX/ALU temp through psnRaReleaseUse/psnRaAssignDefinition
